A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ECVC research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained and revised content.

before.justification: v2 reports original ECVC compression results, complexity measurements, component ablations and finetuning analyses in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds ECVC-FM evaluations and expanded controlled ablations.

M1.justification: New Appendix B introduces ECVC-FM, incorporating ECVC techniques into a DCVC-FM backbone with modified temporal-context channel dimensions. The original DCVC-DC-based ECVC, MNLC, MHLCA and PCFS procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions train on Vimeo-90K and BVI-DVC and evaluate on HEVC B/C/D/E, UVG and MCL-JCV. The new models and controls retain the existing video-compression tasks and short/long coding-chain scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds the enlarged DCVC-DC baseline and DCVC-HEM comparisons with and without PCFS. DCVC-HEM already appeared in the benchmark comparisons, but its participation in these controlled ablations is new. The main benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added ablations introduce a 60M-parameter control through proportional channel expansion and evaluate additional PCFS/component configurations. ECVC-FM introduces another model configuration. Existing splits, preprocessing, metrics, intra periods and 96-frame/all-frame evaluation protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Table 6 substantially expands the analysis: the enlarged baseline tests whether capacity explains MNLC gains, PCFS-only configurations isolate finetuning benefits, and DCVC-HEM tests transfer to another codec. The previous NLC-without-PCFS rows are removed and NLC-with-PCFS rows added. The noise, attention-visualization and finetuning-length analyses otherwise remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new Table 6 average column summarizes performance across datasets and does not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v3 adds ECVC-FM results across six benchmark groups: average BD-rates are reported as -32.3%, -32.3% and -33.4% in Tables 8, 10 and 11. Table 6 adds substantial capacity-control and PCFS results, while replacing the standalone NLC entries with different configurations. Original ECVC benchmark scores remain unchanged. Five VTM MS-SSIM curves are removed from Figure 15.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 retains the same normalized-attention property and algebraic proof. Its revised wording, explicit row-index range and closing sentence do not change the mathematics. The remaining equations and derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the non-local-context and PCFS contributions, novelty claim and headline ECVC performance claims. ECVC-FM is introduced in the appendix without redefining these central claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 newly attributes longer-sequence finetuning gains to diverse error patterns improving generalization. The appendix removes speculation that access to official DCVC training strategies could further improve performance. The existing limitation concerning out-of-domain videos, including anime, remains.

D1.justification: The code statement changes from forthcoming to available at the same repository. v3 also documents the enlarged baseline's channel-scaling rule, ECVC-FM's 53.05M parameters and the query-based attention-visualization procedure. Existing training details and VTM commands are retained; exact ECVC-FM channel dimensions are not supplied.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to UCVC, Adaptive Prediction Structure for Learned Video Compression, and Hybrid Local-Global Context Learning for Neural Video Compression. These modestly expand the introduction's coverage without substantively changing the related-work narrative or novelty positioning.

P1.justification: Editing is localized to proof wording, attention-visualization explanation, author contact information and a shortened appendix results discussion. Adding the ECVC-FM subsection changes the appendix organization from A–C to A–D; the main narrative structure remains.

P2.justification: Table 6 gains control blocks and an average column; Tables 8, 10 and 11 gain ECVC-FM rows. Figures 12–14 add ECVC-FM curves, Figure 14 also adds VTM curves, and Figure 15 removes VTM curves except for HEVC C. Several figures and tables are resized or relocated within the retained layout.

improvement.justification: The new capacity control and PCFS-only/DCVC-HEM ablations strengthen attribution of the reported gains beyond v2's component comparisons. The updated code-availability statement also improves access information. These benefits are limited by sparse ECVC-FM documentation and unexplained identical ECVC-FM rows in Tables 8 and 10 despite different intra-period settings. The original scientific claims and benchmark results are largely retained.
